intervention_label: One block-release request carrying tissue orders A, B and C, plus a documented ECOG with altitude-referenced oximetry, baseline echocardiogram and organ-function labs — diagnostic gate
expected_benefit: Resolves, on one block release: INI1/SMARCB1 by IHC on both the 2024 uterine specimen and the 2026 lung core (opens or closes the EZH2 branch), Rb by IHC (routes NCT06498648 vs NCT07633756), MMR, p53, ATRX, PD-L1 and B7-H3, tissue NGS with an HRD/genomic-instability score and HRR gene set, TMB, RNA fusion calling, and MAGE-A4 / PRAME / NY-ESO-1 antigen expression. The clinic half returns a scored ECOG, resting and ambulatory oximetry recorded at 8,500 ft, an LVEF, and hepatic, renal and haematologic baselines.
key_risks: No therapeutic toxicity; the risk is calendar. Block release from the 2024 outside institution is the rate-limiting step and nobody clinical owns it
Ordering the three tissue requisitions serially rather than on one release spends the first-line window on paperwork
Antigen-expression IHC (order C) is not reliably covered outside a trial; ask self-pay pricing and ask sponsors whether they run their own assay
preference_alignment: Forecloses nothing and costs nothing on any preference axis; it is the one item that survives whatever she answers about trials, travel and toxicity. Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES, because the same results feed standard-care decisions either way.
guideline_status: Not a guideline item as such; every eligibility bound the board cited (ECOG 0-1 at NCT03880019 and NCT03686124, ECOG 0-1 in LMS-04 itself, baseline LVEF before an anthracycline per ASCO and ESC cardio-oncology) assumes measurements this chart does not contain.
rationale_summary: This row exists because the board split over whether a measurement belongs in a therapeutic ranking, and both sides were right about different things. The advocate ranked a scored ECOG first; the critic conceded the applicability point out loud, that every effect estimate quoted in this case comes from trials enrolling ECOG 0-1, so an unmeasured score is a defect inside the numbers rather than an administrative chore, then objected structurally that a measurement has no effect size or comparator and ranking it makes the slate non-comparable. The shared workup slot is the mechanism that settles it: the gate sits at rank 1 without competing with a therapy for the same seat. Its content is the union of what all five personas kept demanding under every pick, and its access_route reads standard_of_care because these are pathology requisitions and a clinic visit that any treating team can place this week, with no protocol or label involved. Three tissue orders cover nearly every open question in this case, and block release from the 2024 outside institution is what actually gates them.
open_questions: Whether MD Anderson accepts an outside CLIA Rb result or must run its own G3-245 assay, which changes the screening timeline
Whether the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 pulmonary core will be discordant for INI1; the shedding compartment is the lung, not a uterus removed in 2024
Whether paired buffy-coat sequencing or tissue NGS settles TP53 Q52* as tumour-derived or clonal haematopoiesis, which also bears on how much the plasma SMARCB1 call is worth
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic gate: one block release resolves INI1, Rb, HRD/HRR, MMR, TMB, fusions and three antigen stains; the clinic half returns ECOG, LVEF and altitude-read oximetry.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — pathology orders on archival tissue plus a clinic visit and an echocardiogram)

counter_productive_moa.description: Diagnostic and clinical measurement; no therapeutic mechanism.

overall: One block release and one clinic visit decide six downstream branches, and the 2024 outside institution that signed the primary out benign is the bottleneck.

intervention_label: Olaparib + temozolomide (NCI Protocol 10250 regimen in uterine leiomyosarcoma), post-induction, with tissue HRD/HRR testing ordered now
expected_benefit: Overall best ORR 27% (6 of 22; the prespecified primary-endpoint ORR was 23%) and mPFS 6.9 months (95% CI 5.4-NE) in advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after at least one prior line. The prespecified endpoint was met. Entry did not require HRD.
key_risks: Grade 3/4 neutropenia 75% and thrombocytopenia 32%, arriving in a marrow that will have just absorbed LMS-04's 80% and 47%
n=22, single-arm, open-label response assessment (ROBINS-I moderate); the randomised confirmation is accrued but unreported
Off-label prescription is the only live route; both trials of the combination are closed to accrual
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7: PARTIAL — the efficacy signal is the best lineage-matched one in the file, but a second consecutive 75% grade 3/4 neutropenia is a toxicity question nobody has put to her. Matches prefers_trials: NO — both trials are closed, so this is an off-label prescription, not a seat. Empty toxicity_vetoes cannot be read as consent here.
guideline_status: Ahead of settled carriage. The ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS CPG 2021 (pmid:34303806) predates the trial, and the concensusite could not confirm NCCN listing this run because NCCN blocked automated access. That gap is why it sat at rank 4 rather than rank 2 on the guideline chair's own slate.
rationale_summary: Four of five personas ranked this, and they ranked it for the same reason: it is the strongest targeted signal anyone has produced in her exact histology, and it is the one pick where ordering tissue now changes a decision made later. The critic and the concensusite both rested it on the prespecified endpoint rather than on the RAD51 split, and the critic's discipline on that point is worth carrying: 11.2 versus 5.4 months at p=0.05 in 18 assayed patients is exploratory and must not be quoted as a result. The risktaker took the subgroup bet explicitly and said so, which is how a subgroup ought to be carried. Entry required a prior line, so this cannot fill the first-line window; what can fill it is the tissue HRD and HRR order that makes the later off-label authorisation winnable. Nobody dissented and nobody vetoed. The load-bearing unknown is her own homologous-recombination status, and it is unmeasured because the plasma panel could not settle it at unstated tumour fraction.
open_questions: Her HRD/HRR and BRCA2 status, unmeasured; the 4-patient BRCA2 series (pmid:30541756) is tier 4 and cannot carry a selection claim
Whether the randomised phase 2/3 (nct:NCT05432791), fully accrued and unreported, deflates the single-arm response rate
Whether marrow reserve after six cycles of LMS-04 tolerates a regimen that produced 75% grade 3/4 neutropenia in chemotherapy-pretreated patients
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate in her exact histology: ORR 27% (6 of 22) and mPFS 6.9 months in advanced uterine LMS, prespecified endpoint met (pmid:37467452).
toxicity_burden: High (G3/4 neutropenia 75%, thrombocytopenia 32%, anaemia; managed with dose modification, no treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: Overlapping myelosuppression after LMS-04 may force dose reductions that cost the PARP exposure the regimen depends on.

overall: The best lineage-matched targeted signal in this file, sitting one line away and worth ordering tissue HRD for now — at a heavy second consecutive marrow cost.

intervention_label: Abemaciclib + gemcitabine and docetaxel (NCT06498648, MD Anderson randomised phase 1/2), Rb-intact required
expected_benefit: No efficacy readout exists for the combination; the phase 1 endpoint is a blood thymidine kinase activity time course. What the design buys is a floor: the randomised phase 2 compares against the gemcitabine/docetaxel backbone itself, which produced ORR 35.8% (95% CI 23.5-49.6) first line in metastatic uterine LMS in the GOG phase 2 (pmid:18534250).
key_risks: Overlapping myelosuppression is uncharacterised outside this study's own phase 1 portion; abemaciclib's diarrhoea and neutropenia layer onto a myelosuppressive doublet
Backbone toxicity from the uterine phase 2: G3 anaemia 24%, G3 fatigue 17%, G3-4 neutropenia 17%, and one possibly related grade 4 pulmonary event in 42 patients
Single site in Houston; screening turnaround has to beat the LMS-04 start date
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES, and it is the only investigational seat that honours it without spending the first-line window, because LMS-04 contains no gemcitabine. Matches modality_constraints: UNKNOWN — an empty list is not the same as a woman at 8,500 ft agreeing to fly to Houston, and the advocate's dissent on exactly this point stands.
guideline_status: No guideline carries the combination. The gemcitabine/docetaxel control arm is the long-standing NCCN soft tissue sarcoma option in leiomyosarcoma, which is what the concensusite endorsed from the guideline chair.
rationale_summary: Four personas ranked this and the fifth endorsed it inside its own gemcitabine/docetaxel row, so the board is close to unanimous on the seat while being frank that the drug is unproven. The design is what earns it: the randomised phase 2 arm is the standard backbone, so the worst case inside the trial is guideline care, which is not true of any other investigational seat here. Its quiet virtue is sequencing — the phase 2 admits systemic-treatment-naive patients and the disqualifier is prior gemcitabine, which LMS-04 does not contain, so this branch survives induction while an off-protocol gemcitabine/docetaxel prescription would close it permanently. The critic ranked it fourth and named the real cost out loud: abemaciclib has essentially no efficacy data in leiomyosarcoma, and taking the seat first line trades a phase 3 OS result for an unvalidated add-on. Eligibility rests on a stain nobody has done. One Rb IHC routes her here if Rb is intact and toward the CDK7 protocol (nct:NCT07633756) if Rb is lost, and it is already on the planned block cut.
open_questions: Whether the treatment-naive stratum is currently open, and whether MD Anderson accepts an outside CLIA Rb result or must run its own assay
Whether abemaciclib's G1 arrest antagonises the S-phase-dependent gemcitabine it is layered onto; the study's phase 1 is where that is first characterised
Whether she can and wants to travel to Houston during first-line treatment, a question nobody has asked her
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown for the add-on: no abemaciclib efficacy data in LMS. The floor is the randomised gem/doc control arm, ORR 35.8% first-line uterine (pmid:18534250).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (backbone G3 anaemia 24%, G3 fatigue 17%, G3-4 neutropenia 17%, one G4 pulmonary event in 42; abemaciclib diarrhoea uncharacterised on this doublet)

counter_productive_moa.description: CDK4/6-induced G1 arrest can antagonise S-phase-dependent gemcitabine; Rb-intact status, the premise of the whole seat, is unmeasured.

overall: The one investigational seat that survives LMS-04 instead of competing with it, routed by a single Rb stain and carrying no efficacy data of its own.

intervention_label: IMA203 / IMA203CD8 PRAME-directed TCR-T cells (NCT03686124), sponsor screening started in the first-line window
expected_benefit: Confirmed ORR 28.9% with MTD not reached in a 41-patient first-in-human phase 1 across PRAME-positive HLA-A*02-positive solid tumours, melanoma-dominant. Median duration of response 4.4 months (range 2.4-23.0). No uterine leiomyosarcoma patient appears in the published dataset.
key_risks: Severe cytokine release syndrome in 2 of 41 (4.9%); no severe neurotoxicity reported; lymphodepletion cytopenias expected but not tabulated per term
Protocol requires ECOG 0-1 and receipt of, or ineligibility for, all available indicated standard-of-care treatment — a clause that likely puts this after induction
Cell-therapy screening in this class asks for room-air saturation of at least 90%, and one neighbouring protocol excludes below 92%; at 8,500 ft an unannotated oximetry reading is what fails her
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES. Matches modality_constraints: UNKNOWN — apheresis, lymphodepletion and manufacturing lead time are a different proposition from a tablet, and no one has asked her. The advocate's objection is on the record: holding this seat because a durable-tail outcome is worth chasing is a preference, and it is the risktaker's, not hers.
guideline_status: No guideline recognition in sarcoma for any PRAME-directed product.
rationale_summary: Only the risktaker ranked this, and the critic dissented hard on evidence quality: 28.9% is a phase 1 number with no uterine LMS patient in it, median response duration is 4.4 months, and the premise that PRAME is the likeliest of the three antigens to return positive has nothing under it in this file. The one prevalence series carried here covers 26 smooth-muscle tumours, is not uterus-restricted, quotes no smooth-muscle PRAME figure at all, and its neighbouring MAGE-A4 number drew an erratum. The advocate qualified rather than endorsed, objecting to the warrant rather than the biology, which is why this reads as considered_with_caveats rather than a clean recommendation despite only one formal dissent. What holds the row on the table is the risktaker's narrower point, which the critic's own erratum objection does not touch: the sponsor's IMADetect RT-qPCR screen takes weeks, runs in parallel with induction, and spends nothing from the LMS-04 window. Her confirmed HLA-A*02:01 is the necessary half of a two-part gate; the antigen stain is the missing half.
open_questions: Whether uterine leiomyosarcoma falls inside the current solid-tumour cohorts, and whether the standard-of-care-exhaustion clause admits a patient who declined first line
PRAME expression, unmeasured, and decided on the sponsor's own RT-qPCR rather than on a local IHC with known operating characteristics
Whether tumour HLA-A*02:01 loss of heterozygosity, unassessed, would undercut every A*02:01-directed option at once
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-uncertain: 28.9% confirmed ORR in a 41-patient phase 1 with no uLMS patient and mDoR 4.4 months (pmid:40205198).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (severe CRS 4.9%, no severe ICANS in n=41; lymphodepletion cytopenias expected but not tabulated per term)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen-loss or HLA-A*02:01 LOH escape; a local PRAME stain has no established operating characteristics against the sponsor assay.

overall: The only cellular axis her confirmed HLA-A*02:01 opens, double-gated on a sponsor PRAME assay and a standard-of-care-exhaustion clause.

intervention_label: In vivo lung perfusion with doxorubicin plus metastasectomy for sarcoma pulmonary metastases (NCT02811523, Toronto), as post-induction consolidation
expected_benefit: No human efficacy data for the perfusion itself; the registered primary endpoint is acute lung injury and the clinical base is a phase 1 built on preclinical work (pmid:26952295). The number the approach is chasing belongs to metastasectomy: 55.4% five-year OS in the uterine-sarcoma subset of a Japanese multicentre registry, selected on a disease-free interval of 12 months or more, and 36% five-year OS after complete resection in the international registry.
key_risks: Thoracotomy morbidity plus acute lung injury from the perfusion, in a lifetime never-smoker with unmeasured pulmonary reserve at an 8,500 ft baseline
Every lesion in the perfused lung must be resectable by wedge or segment, and an infiltrative bilateral pattern is exactly the finding that defeats that judgement
Cumulative doxorubicin above 450 mg excludes; six full LMS-04 cycles at 60 mg/m2 approach it, so the arithmetic belongs before cycle 1
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7: PARTIAL, since 0.7 leans efficacy but this is the highest-morbidity option in the file. Matches modality_constraints: UNKNOWN — a single Toronto site means an international referral, and nobody has asked whether she can travel.
guideline_status: The shelf has consensus footing that the vehicle does not. ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS CPG 2021 (pmid:34303806) carries complete excision of resectable lung metastases as standard local treatment in selected patients, and NCCN soft tissue sarcoma recognises resection of limited pulmonary metastases; the perfusion protocol itself has no society carriage anywhere. Wedge metastasectomy and SBRT are the carried routes and sit in the Standard-of-care table.
rationale_summary: The risktaker ranked this third and called it what it is, a swing at long-term survival rather than an incremental gain, on the argument that lung-only disease plus a roughly 23-month disease-free interval puts her in the favourable selection band the registries describe. The conservative dissented on toxicity: a phase 1 perfusion protocol with no published safety series in this population, asking a patient with unmeasured pulmonary reserve at altitude to hold a thoracotomy seat, and bending a phase 3 regimen's dose intensity around a phase 1 exclusion. The concensusite landed in between, qualified — right shelf, wrong door — and named the carried routes instead. The sharpest objection is the conservative's on selection: 55.4% five-year survival belongs to patients who reached complete resection of countable nodules, and an infiltrative bilateral pattern is the phenotype those series excluded by construction, so her disease-free interval transfers to her and the survival figure does not. The risktaker's counter also stands, that the resectability call belongs to a thoracic surgeon rather than to a radiation-first default made from here. The anthracycline arithmetic is the one part of this that is urgent now rather than later.
open_questions: Whether a thoracic surgeon reads the infiltrative, possibly inflammatory pattern as resectable by wedge, which decides whether this row exists at all
Whether the Toronto protocol accepts US-resident patients, and how the 450 mg cumulative-doxorubicin exclusion is counted against a planned six-cycle induction
Whether the infiltrative radiologic read is tumour or inflammation, which also muddies response assessment during induction
likelihood_of_effect: Uncertain: metastasectomy series give 55.4% five-year OS in resected uterine sarcoma (pmid:37063124), but perfusion itself is phase 1 with no human efficacy readout.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (thoracotomy morbidity; acute lung injury is the trial's registered primary endpoint; no published human safety series in this population)

counter_productive_moa.description: Perfusion injury to already-infiltrated lung; and a full induction spends the anthracycline budget that keeps the door open.

overall: The one option in this dossier aimed at cure rather than control, and the one whose anatomic premise her infiltrative bilateral pattern may defeat.

intervention_label: Ivonescimab (PD-1 x VEGF bispecific), MSK single-arm phase 2 in leiomyosarcoma (NCT07516925)
expected_benefit: No published sarcoma efficacy of any kind. The credibility of the molecule rests on HARMONi-2, where it beat pembrolizumab head to head on PFS in PD-L1-positive NSCLC, HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.38-0.69), mPFS 11.1 vs 5.8 months, at an interim analysis in a China-only trial with immature OS. The MSK study is a 20-patient single-arm phase 2 with an objective-response endpoint.
key_risks: G3+ treatment-related AEs 29% versus 16% for pembrolizumab in NSCLC, the increment mostly VEGF-class effects; G3+ immune-related AEs 7%
All seven sites are in the MSK New York and New Jersey network, six flagged Limited Protocol Activities, and travel is not supplied with the study drug
Prior PD-1, PD-L1 or VEGF-pathway exposure is exclusionary, so starting pazopanib first would close it permanently
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES on paper, and the advocate's own objection is that this is exactly the problem. A defaulted checkbox is doing most of the work behind this rank for a woman who has never been asked whether she wants a trial, or whether repeated flights from a mountain town at 8,500 ft to Manhattan during first-line treatment are livable. Matches modality_constraints: UNKNOWN, for the same reason.
guideline_status: No guideline in any region carries the drug or its class in sarcoma. Approved in China for NSCLC; investigational in the United States.
rationale_summary: This is the only investigational seat in the dossier reachable before cycle 1 by explicit protocol language rather than by inference: patients who decline standard first-line systemic therapy are eligible, and the ECOG ceiling is 2 rather than 0-1. Four of five personas declined it anyway, including the risktaker, and their reason was the same three papers read four times. The critic's convergence verdict belongs on this row: unanimity assembled from one shared evidence base adds no weight, so nobody should bank the 4-to-1 count as extra confidence — but the refusal survives the correction, because GOG-0250, SARC028 and the dedicated uterine LMS futility stop are three mutually independent trials and one of them is a randomised null in this exact disease. Anti-VEGF added to first-line chemotherapy did nothing in uterine LMS (PFS HR 1.12, p=0.58); single-agent PD-1 went 0 for 10 in the LMS cohort of SARC028 and 0 for 12 in the dedicated uLMS study stopped for futility. The advocate ranked it fourth without arguing it was better, and priced it honestly: worth a phone call this week because the seat closes when LMS-04 starts, worth taking only if she says she wants it. Rule-3 tension is live here and unresolved, so the row stays visible with caveats rather than being quietly dropped.
open_questions: Whether the decline-first-line pathway is currently open, what documentation it requires, and which visits could happen at her home institution
Whether MSK patient travel assistance covers a patient flying in from altitude, a question to ask at first contact rather than after the first invoice
Whether she wants a trial at all, which nobody has confirmed with her; if she never did, this rank is wrong
likelihood_of_effect: Low: no sarcoma efficacy data anywhere, and both component axes already failed in uLMS (pmid:25713428, pmid:28440953). HARMONi-2 is an NSCLC result.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ treatment-related AEs 29% in NSCLC, VEGF-class hypertension and bleeding, G3+ immune-related AEs 7%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Both mechanisms have already been beaten in this disease; a spent first-line window is the counter-productive outcome.

overall: The only seat reachable before cycle 1 by explicit protocol language, and the one four of five personas refused on three mutually independent negative trials.

intervention_label: Tazemetostat (EZH2 inhibition for SMARCB1/INI1-deficient disease)
scenario_label: If INI1/SMARCB1 loss is confirmed by IHC on tumour tissue (complete loss of nuclear staining with retained internal control), or biallelic molecular loss where IHC is equivocal
expected_benefit: In the INI1-negative non-epithelioid cohort of the SWI/SNF basket, ORR 9% (3 partial responses of 32). The epithelioid sarcoma registration cohort, a different histology, gave ORR 15% (9 of 62) with mDoR not reached and mPFS 5.5 months. No uterine leiomyosarcoma efficacy data exist anywhere.
key_risks: Unusually gentle for an active oral agent: G3+ treatment-related AEs 10% across 129 patients; G3+ anaemia 6%, weight loss 3%; two treatment-related serious events (one seizure, one haemoptysis)
The branch itself may not exist: 170 of 170 uterine smooth-muscle tumours retained SMARCB1 in the one IHC series, and her call is plasma-only at unstated tumour fraction
Both tazemetostat expanded-access programs are listed as no longer available, and the basket study is closed to accrual
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7: PARTIAL — a 9% cross-histology response rate is a weak efficacy claim, though the toxicity cost is the lowest of any active agent here. Oral, so no infusion chair and no travel.
guideline_status: NCCN recognition is in epithelioid sarcoma. Off-guideline for uterine leiomyosarcoma; any use here is off-label cross-histology extrapolation.
rationale_summary: No persona ranked this and both the critic and the conservative wrote explicit refusals: the stain is worth ordering, the drug is not worth ranking. The honest reading is that SMARCB1 G344Afs*13 is probably a red herring. It is plasma-only, heterozygous, at unsupplied tumour fraction, against a strong prior that uterine smooth-muscle tumours retain INI1, and the TP53 Q52* call that shares its shedding assumptions carries its own clonal-haematopoiesis caveat — if TP53 turns out to be CHIP, the SMARCB1 call's credibility falls with it. The mechanistic chain behind EZH2 inhibition was built in other lineages and needs biallelic loss, and the preclinical file carries the deflating finding that EZH2 dependency in SWI/SNF-mutant cancers is largely non-catalytic. This row is surfaced and gated rather than promising: it becomes real only if INI1 comes back lost on tissue, and even then it buys a 9% response rate on the closest available data. It is flagged thin_evidence because the peer-reviewed efficacy base in her histology is empty and the row is double-gated on a confirmatory stain.
open_questions: Whether INI1 is lost on either specimen; the 2024 uterine block and the 2026 lung core can be discordant and both should be stained
Whether an off-label authorisation is winnable at all given the epithelioid-sarcoma-only approval and closed expanded access
Whether tissue NGS shows biallelic SMARCB1 loss, which is what an equivocal stain would need
likelihood_of_effect: Low even if INI1 is lost: 9% ORR in the INI1-negative non-epithelioid basket cohort, no uLMS patient reported (pmid:41882006).
toxicity_burden: Low (G3+ treatment-related AEs 10%; anaemia 6%, weight loss 3%; two serious events — one seizure, one haemoptysis)

counter_productive_moa.description: EZH2 dependency in SWI/SNF-mutant cancers is largely non-catalytic, so single-agent inhibition may not engage it.

overall: Gated on a stain the board expects to come back retained, and even a positive buys a 9% cross-histology response rate.

intervention_label: REC-617 (selective CDK7 inhibitor) in RB1-negative leiomyosarcoma (NCT07633756, MD Anderson)
expected_benefit: No efficacy data. Phase 1b, n=15, registered primary endpoint is safety and adverse events.
key_risks: Entry requires RB1-negative by IHC at a 0% cutoff and at least one prior systemic line; her Rb status is unmeasured
Single site in Houston; ECOG ceiling 2, which is unusually forgiving
No published toxicity profile for this agent in sarcoma
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES. Travel and modality questions are the same ones nobody has asked about the abemaciclib seat.
rationale_summary: The other side of the same Rb stain. One IHC read routes her: intact Rb points to the abemaciclib randomised phase 1/2 she is eligible for today, Rb loss points here after a first line. Nobody on the board ranked it, and it is flagged thin_evidence because it has no efficacy readout of any kind — a 15-patient phase 1b with a safety endpoint. It earns a row because the stain that opens it is already on the block cut, so the eligibility question can be answered for free while the LMS-04 decision is being made.
open_questions: Whether Rb is lost on tissue; a plasma panel reporting no RB1 alteration settles nothing at unstated tumour fraction
Whether the site accepts an outside CLIA Rb result
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: 15-patient phase 1b with a safety primary endpoint and no efficacy readout.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no published sarcoma toxicity profile; CDK7-class myelosuppression and gastrointestinal toxicity expected)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection raised; the risk is a null first-in-class readout rather than antagonism.

overall: The Rb-loss half of a single stain that also routes the abemaciclib seat — free to answer now, with no efficacy data behind it.

intervention_label: CDR404 (MAGE-A4 x CD3 T-cell engager) in HLA-A*02:01, MAGE-A4-expressing solid tumours (NCT06402201)
expected_benefit: No efficacy data. First-in-human phase 1, n=42, registered primary endpoint is dose-limiting toxicity.
key_risks: MAGE-A4 expression unmeasured, and the one smooth-muscle prevalence figure in the file is internally inconsistent and carries an erratum
ECOG 0-1 required against a score nobody has written down
T-cell-engager cytokine release syndrome risk, no grade profile published
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES. An antibody-format engager needs no apheresis and no manufacturing lead time, which is a real practical difference from the TCR-T products for a patient who has not started chemotherapy.
rationale_summary: The risktaker flagged this as a free parallel call: MAGE-A4 IHC rides the same tissue order as PRAME, so asking whether uterine leiomyosarcoma is on the selected-tumours list costs nothing. Recruiting with US sites, and its registry text does not obviously require a prior line, which makes it one of very few investigational routes possibly reachable in the first-line window. Flagged thin_evidence: a first-in-human phase 1 with a dose-limiting-toxicity endpoint and no published efficacy, gated on an unmeasured antigen.
open_questions: Whether a systemic-therapy-naive patient can enrol, and which US sites are screening
What MAGE-A4 assay and cutoff the study uses, and whether a local IHC is accepted for pre-screening
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: first-in-human phase 1 with a dose-limiting-toxicity endpoint and no efficacy readout; MAGE-A4 status unmeasured.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (T-cell-engager CRS risk; no published grade profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen-loss and HLA LOH escape possible; no data either way in this histology.

overall: An off-the-shelf MAGE-A4 engager with no manufacturing lead time and possibly no prior-line requirement, but zero efficacy data and an unstained antigen.

intervention_label: B7-H3-directed antibody-drug conjugates (MGC026, GSK5764227 / HS-20093)
expected_benefit: No sarcoma efficacy data from either recruiting programme; both are dose-escalation studies with adverse-event endpoints. The target rationale is prevalence: 97% of soft tissue sarcoma specimens positive and about 69% high in a 153-patient series spanning 15 subtypes including leiomyosarcoma.
key_risks: Neither study requires a B7-H3 result to enrol, so a stain informs rather than gates; the ADC payload toxicities are uncharacterised in sarcoma
Both require progression on available standard therapy, so they open after induction
The first randomised phase 3 of a B7-H3 ADC in sarcoma is osteosarcoma-only and she cannot enrol in it
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES. US, UK, Australian and Canadian sites, so this is the least geographically constrained of the investigational surface targets.
rationale_summary: B7-H3 has the best odds of a positive stain of any surface target in this case, and the IHC rides the same block cut as INI1 and MMR, so the question can be closed for almost nothing. No persona ranked the class. Flagged thin_evidence because both accessible programmes are dose-escalation phase 1 studies with no sarcoma efficacy readout, and the one randomised test of the mechanism in a sarcoma is restricted to osteosarcoma.
open_questions: B7-H3 expression, unmeasured
Whether the sarcoma cohorts of either US-accessible programme are open at the point she needs them
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: dose-escalation phase 1 programmes with no sarcoma efficacy readout; target prevalence is high (97% positive, pmid:39478506) but unmeasured here.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (ADC-class myelosuppression, interstitial lung disease risk; no sarcoma-specific grade profile published)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen-density threshold effects could blunt payload delivery; no mechanism objection raised by the board.

overall: The surface target most likely to be present, riding a stain that costs almost nothing — but every accessible programme is a phase 1 with no efficacy data.

intervention_label: Peposertib (DNA-PK inhibitor) + low-dose pegylated liposomal doxorubicin (NCT05711615), anthracycline-ceiling-gated
expected_benefit: No efficacy readout; the registered endpoints are safety and a recommended phase 2 dose. Leiomyosarcoma is a named eligible histology.
key_risks: Prior anthracycline is permitted only if cumulative dose before enrolment stays at or under 360 mg/m2 — exactly six full LMS-04 cycles at 60 mg/m2
Requires at least one prior line, so it opens after induction
No published toxicity profile for the combination
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES; 16 US sites including one within reach of a mountain-state patient. ECOG ceiling 2.
rationale_summary: The reason this row is not merely a later-line footnote is arithmetic that is urgent now. Three personas independently flagged that six cycles at 60 mg/m2 lands exactly on this protocol's 360 mg/m2 ceiling, and the in-vivo lung perfusion protocol excludes above 450 mg cumulative. Both ceilings belong in the induction conversation before cycle 1, not before cycle 6. Flagged thin_evidence: a recruiting phase 1 with a dose-finding endpoint and nothing published on efficacy.
open_questions: How the treating team plans to count cumulative doxorubicin, and whether a stopping rule is written before induction starts
Whether the trial's line requirement is satisfied by LMS-04 alone
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: recruiting phase 1 with a dose-finding endpoint and no efficacy readout in any histology.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (DNA-PK inhibitor plus anthracycline; myelosuppression and mucositis expected, no published grade profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: Radiosensitiser-class mechanism with no antagonism vector raised; the risk is a spent anthracycline budget.

overall: A later-line seat whose 360 mg/m2 anthracycline ceiling makes it an induction-planning question rather than a progression question.

intervention_label: ADCE-D01 (uPARAP/Endo180-directed antibody-drug conjugate) in soft-tissue sarcoma (NCT06797999)
expected_benefit: No efficacy data; phase 1/2 first-in-human with maximum tolerated dose and recommended phase 2 dose as endpoints.
key_risks: Requires one to two prior cytotoxic lines for metastatic disease, so the window opens after induction and closes if she accumulates a third line
ECOG 0-1 required against an unmeasured score
ADC payload toxicities uncharacterised
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES; US and Western European sites.
rationale_summary: A sarcoma-dedicated ADC taking any histology after one to two prior cytotoxic lines, so LMS-04 alone would qualify her. No board persona ranked it. The narrow line window is the thing worth marking on a calendar now rather than discovering at third progression. Flagged thin_evidence: first-in-human, dose-finding, no efficacy readout.
open_questions: Which US sites are screening and what the slot situation looks like six months out
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: first-in-human dose-escalation with no efficacy readout.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (ADC-class myelosuppression and payload effects; no published grade profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection raised; risk is a null first-in-human readout.

overall: A sarcoma-dedicated ADC with a line window that LMS-04 opens and a third line would close — worth a calendar entry, not a rank.

intervention_label: ZL-6201 (LRRC15-directed antibody-drug conjugate) in sarcoma (NCT07374848)
expected_benefit: No efficacy data; phase 1 with a dose-limiting-toxicity endpoint.
key_risks: ECOG ceiling 1, the strictest in this tier, against an unmeasured score
Up to two prior systemic lines in the metastatic setting, so the window closes after a third
Mandatory pre-treatment biopsy or archival block, which the block-release request should already have solved
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES; US and China sites, US sites reachable.
rationale_summary: Same shape as the other first-in-human ADCs here: a post-induction seat with a line ceiling that eventually closes it, and a mandatory archival block that the rank-1 release request covers. Nobody ranked it. Flagged thin_evidence for the same reason as its class-mates — a dose-limiting-toxicity endpoint and no efficacy readout.
open_questions: Which US sites are open, and whether LRRC15 expression is required or only collected
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: phase 1 dose-escalation with no efficacy readout.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (ADC-class myelosuppression and payload effects; no published grade profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection raised; risk is a null first-in-human readout.

overall: A post-induction ADC seat with the strictest performance-status ceiling in this tier and no efficacy data.

intervention_label: Gemcitabine + nab-sirolimus in leiomyosarcoma or TSC1/TSC2-altered sarcoma (NCT06308419)
expected_benefit: No efficacy data; phase 1, n=18, safety and adverse events as the registered endpoint.
key_risks: Requires one prior systemic therapy, so it opens after induction
Gemcitabine here would close the abemaciclib seat permanently, the same sequencing conflict the board flagged for off-protocol gem/doc
Single site in Houston
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES. Nab-sirolimus separately carries a registered expanded-access protocol nationally for malignancies with mTOR-pathway alterations, so a TSC finding on tissue order A would open a second route.
rationale_summary: Leiomyosarcoma patients enter on histology alone without needing a TSC alteration, and the ECOG ceiling is 2. Nobody on the board ranked it. Two things make it worth surfacing: TSC1 and TSC2 are standard content on the comprehensive panel already being ordered, and a positive would open a national expanded-access route independent of the trial. Flagged thin_evidence: an 18-patient phase 1 with a safety endpoint.
open_questions: TSC1/TSC2 status, which tissue order A will report at no extra cost
Whether taking this seat is worth closing the abemaciclib trial by giving gemcitabine
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: 18-patient phase 1 with a safety endpoint and no efficacy readout.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (gemcitabine myelosuppression plus mTOR-inhibitor stomatitis and metabolic effects; no published combination profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: Gemcitabine exposure here permanently forecloses the abemaciclib randomised seat — a sequencing cost, not an antagonism.

overall: A post-induction phase 1 whose gemcitabine backbone would permanently close the one trial seat LMS-04 preserves.

intervention_label: All-trans retinoic acid + cemiplimab in leiomyosarcoma after standard chemotherapy (NCT06528769)
expected_benefit: No efficacy data; phase 2, n=16, overall response rate as the endpoint.
key_risks: The checkpoint component carries the same negative record this histology has already produced: 0 of 12 in the dedicated uLMS study stopped for futility
Requires prior standard-of-care chemotherapy, so it opens after induction
Single site in Columbus
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES. Both components are approved drugs, so an off-label version is technically prescribable, though without evidence or payer support.
rationale_summary: The mechanistic idea here is not the checkpoint antibody but the retinoid: PRAME acts as a dominant repressor of retinoic-acid receptor signalling, which is the one rationale in the file for pairing ATRA with PD-1 blockade in a PRAME-expressing tumour. Nobody ranked it. Flagged thin_evidence: a 16-patient single-arm phase 2 with no readout, resting on a checkpoint component this disease has already defeated twice.
open_questions: Whether PRAME expression is being collected on this study, which would make the tissue-order-C stain do double duty
Whether the cohort is still open after a first line
likelihood_of_effect: Low: 16-patient single-arm phase 2 with no readout, built on a checkpoint component that went 0 of 12 in dedicated uLMS (pmid:28440953).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (immune-related toxicity plus retinoid effects — hypertriglyceridaemia, mucocutaneous dryness, headache; no published combination profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: Single-agent PD-1 has failed twice in this histology; the retinoid rationale is preclinical and PRAME-dependent.

overall: The one PRAME-adjacent rationale that does not need a cell product, attached to a checkpoint backbone this disease has already beaten twice.

intervention_label: Pulmonary suffusion with cisplatin plus metastasectomy for sarcoma lung metastases (NCT03965234, Roswell Park)
expected_benefit: No efficacy data; phase 1/2 with local toxicity incidence as the registered endpoint.
key_risks: Presumes resectable pulmonary disease, which her infiltrative bilateral pattern puts in doubt
Requires a surgeon's judgement that pulmonary function supports the planned metastasectomy, and no PFTs exist
Single site in Buffalo
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES. ECOG ceiling 2 and no prior-line requirement in the registry criteria, which makes it unusually permissive on the axes that block other seats.
guideline_status: The metastasectomy component sits under ESMO and NCCN carriage for complete excision of resectable lung metastases in selected patients; the suffusion technique itself has no society carriage.
rationale_summary: The US-side counterpart to the Toronto perfusion protocol, aimed at minimal residual disease in the lung after metastasectomy, and it does not require a prior line. Nobody on the board ranked it, but the risktaker's charge that the slate under-weighted the locoregional swing applies here as much as to the Toronto row. It rests on the same premise, and that premise is the same thing that may defeat it: an infiltrative bilateral pattern is not a resection target today. Flagged thin_evidence — a phase 1/2 with a local-toxicity endpoint.
open_questions: Whether a thoracic surgeon reads her current pattern as within the resectable population
Whether pulmonary reserve at an 8,500 ft baseline supports the planned operation
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: phase 1/2 with a local-toxicity endpoint; the survival rationale belongs to metastasectomy series, not to suffusion (pmid:9011700).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (thoracotomy morbidity plus regional cisplatin exposure; no published outcome series)

counter_productive_moa.description: Same resectability premise as the Toronto protocol; an infiltrative bilateral pattern may never qualify.

overall: The US locoregional trial with no prior-line requirement, resting on a resectability judgement her current imaging may not support.

intervention_label: Tuvusertib (ATR inhibitor) + temozolomide, NCI dose escalation (NCT05691491)
expected_benefit: No efficacy data; the registered endpoints are safety and a recommended phase 2 dose.
key_risks: The monotherapy form of this hypothesis already failed in her histology: an ATRX-mutant leiomyosarcoma cohort progressed within 4 months despite biopsy-proven target engagement
Requires progression on, intolerance of, or refusal of available therapies, so it opens after induction
No published toxicity profile for the combination
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES; 23 US sites and an ECOG ceiling of 2 make it the most reachable ATR seat in the file.
rationale_summary: The one live US seat the ATR sweep found. Its dose-escalation arm admits soft-tissue sarcoma without an MGMT result because temozolomide is guideline-standard in the histology. Nobody ranked it, and the reason is that the ALT/ATR thesis was tested in her exact disease and lost: SLFN11, not ATRX, tracked with benefit in that study. Flagged thin_evidence — a dose-finding study with no efficacy readout, carrying a mechanism the histology has already answered once in the negative.
open_questions: ATRX status, unmeasured, which tissue order A will report
Whether the randomised berzosertib plus gemcitabine leiomyosarcoma study, accrued and unreported, changes the class verdict
likelihood_of_effect: Low: the monotherapy form of this hypothesis failed in ATRX-mutant LMS with target engagement proven on biopsy (pmid:39453756).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (ATR-inhibitor plus alkylator myelosuppression; no published combination grade profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: ALT-selective ATR sensitivity failed to replicate, and the sarcoma cohort testing it progressed within four months.

overall: The only reachable ATR seat, carrying a hypothesis this histology has already tested and answered in the negative.

intervention_label: FAP-directed radioligand therapy ([225Ac]RTX-2358, [212Pb]Pb-PSV359, [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286)
expected_benefit: No efficacy data in sarcoma from any of the three programmes; all are phase 1 or 1/2 with safety or dose-limiting-toxicity endpoints.
key_risks: Each gates on a positive FAP imaging scan rather than on tissue, and that scan is not routine outside the protocols
All require prior lines; the alpha-emitter study asks for relapsed and refractory disease
Radioligand marrow toxicity on a marrow already hit by induction
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES; US, Canadian, Australian and Western European sites.
rationale_summary: Three recruiting programmes, all with US sites, all selecting on imaging uptake rather than histology, which makes FAP one of the few targets in this dossier where the screening test is a scan rather than a stain. Nobody ranked it. Flagged thin_evidence: no sarcoma efficacy readout anywhere in the class, and the imaging gate itself is only available inside the protocols.
open_questions: Whether her tumour takes up an FAP tracer, which is unknowable until one of the protocols scans her
Whether the tumour-type cohorts are still open at the point she would need them
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: three phase 1 or 1/2 programmes with safety endpoints and no sarcoma efficacy readout.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (radioligand marrow suppression and renal exposure; no sarcoma-specific grade profile published)

counter_productive_moa.description: Stromal FAP targeting has no antagonism vector raised; the risk is absent uptake.

overall: The one axis whose screening test is a scan rather than a stain, with no sarcoma efficacy data behind any of its three programmes.

intervention_label: Zanzalintinib (XL092), next-generation multikinase inhibitor with a leiomyosarcoma cohort (NCT06571734)
expected_benefit: No readout yet; phase 2, n=73, progression-free survival as the endpoint. The class benchmark is pazopanib: PFS 4.6 vs 1.6 months against placebo, HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.24-0.40), with no OS gain and an 11% response rate in the uterine-specific retrospective read.
key_risks: Requires at least two prior lines of antineoplastic treatment; she has none
Single US site in Chicago, with pathology review required at an NCCN-designated centre
Antiangiogenic class toxicity interacts with an infiltrative lung pattern
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: YES in principle, but not enrollable for at least two lines.
guideline_status: The class ancestor pazopanib is an NCCN soft tissue sarcoma option after prior chemotherapy and lives in the Standard-of-care table; zanzalintinib has no carriage.
rationale_summary: A third-line conversation at the earliest, which is why it is flagged not_enrollable rather than ranked. Worth naming now for one practical reason: the required NCCN-designated-centre pathology review is exactly the kind of administrative step that takes months, and her original specimen has already been re-reviewed once. Arranging it early costs nothing.
open_questions: Whether the leiomyosarcoma cohort is still open in two lines' time
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: phase 2 with no readout. Class benchmark pazopanib gives roughly three months of PFS with no OS gain (pmid:22595799).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (VEGFR-TKI class: hypertension, fatigue, diarrhoea, hand-foot syndrome; no agent-specific sarcoma profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antiangiogenic wound-healing impairment would conflict with any planned metastasectomy; sequencing issue, not antagonism.

overall: A third-line seat at the earliest, worth naming now only because its pathology-review requirement takes months to arrange.

intervention_label: Lurbinectedin + doxorubicin, first-line anthracycline-naive leiomyosarcoma (SaLuDo, NCT06088290)
expected_benefit: No published result; phase 3, n=469, progression-free survival by independent review. Accrual is closed.
key_risks: No compendium support for off-label use in sarcoma while the phase 3 read-out is unpublished
Lurbinectedin's approval is in small cell lung cancer, so a payer request has nothing to anchor on
Same DNA-minor-groove mechanism as the trabectedin she is planned to receive
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO, because the trial that would have fitted her almost perfectly has stopped enrolling.
rationale_summary: The near-miss of this case: a first-line anthracycline-naive leiomyosarcoma phase 3 that matched her indication and line exactly, and closed to accrual before she was diagnosed correctly. Nobody ranked it. Flagged not_enrollable rather than dropped, because a reader scanning the trial landscape will find it and should see why it is not an option, and because its read-out is one of the few things that could change the first-line calculus in this disease.
open_questions: Whether accrual is truly closed rather than paused; the registry status reads active, not recruiting
When the phase 3 reports, and whether it displaces the LMS-04 comparison
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: phase 3 accrued and unreported; no efficacy data public.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (trabectedin-class myelosuppression and transaminitis expected; no combination profile published)

counter_productive_moa.description: Mechanistically redundant with the trabectedin already planned in induction.

overall: The trial that matched her indication and line exactly and closed before her diagnosis was corrected — a read-out to watch, not a seat.

intervention_label: Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin maintenance after first-line chemotherapy (MELODY, NCT06981637)
expected_benefit: No readout; phase 2, n=81, progression-free survival from randomisation. LMS-04 already answers the same maintenance question with trabectedin.
key_risks: The trial is Taiwan-only
Cumulative anthracycline exposure from LMS-04 induction constrains any further anthracycline maintenance
Off-label maintenance in soft-tissue sarcoma has no guideline backing
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO, on geography.
rationale_summary: The maintenance question this study asks is the one LMS-04's own trabectedin maintenance phase already answers for her, and the trial is Taiwan-only. Nobody ranked it. Flagged not_enrollable and parked until the maintenance phase is actually live, when the cumulative-anthracycline ceiling already flagged for other seats becomes the binding consideration.
open_questions: Whether any anthracycline maintenance is compatible with the cumulative dose LMS-04 will already have delivered
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown: phase 2 with no readout, and the same question is answered inside her planned regimen (pmid:35835135).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (liposomal anthracycline: palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, mucositis, myelosuppression)

counter_productive_moa.description: Further anthracycline exposure erodes the cumulative-dose headroom that two other protocols gate on.

overall: A maintenance question her planned regimen already answers, in a trial she cannot reach.

intervention_label: Anlotinib (catequentinib, AL3818) in refractory soft-tissue sarcoma (APROMISS, NCT03016819)
expected_benefit: ORR 13% (95% CI 7.6-18) overall in a 166-patient single-arm phase 2 in refractory STS, with mPFS 5.6 months overall and 11 months in the 26-patient leiomyosarcoma subset. The subset was not prespecified for inference and carries no uterine breakdown.
key_risks: Cleanest VEGFR-TKI toxicity profile in this space, but G3+ pneumothorax at 2.4% deserves attention in bilateral lung disease
The leiomyosarcoma arm of the phase 3 is marked closed with new recruitment to that indication suspended
Requires at least one prior line and ECOG 0-1; Chinese population, so the subgroup result may not transfer
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO in practice, because the arm that would take her is suspended.
guideline_status: Not approved in the US or EU.
rationale_summary: The 26-patient leiomyosarcoma subset did unusually well, an 11-month median PFS that no other VEGFR-TKI in this file approaches, which is exactly the kind of number that should not be acted on: not prespecified, no uterine breakdown, Chinese population. Nobody ranked it. Flagged not_enrollable because the leiomyosarcoma indication is suspended on the registry and only the broader any-sarcoma indication remains open. Worth one email to ask whether it has reopened.
open_questions: Whether the leiomyosarcoma indication has reopened, and whether the broader indication would accept her
Whether the LMS subset signal survives a prespecified test anywhere
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-uncertain: ORR 13% overall with an 11-month mPFS in a 26-patient LMS subset that was not prespecified for inference (pmid:29895706).
toxicity_burden: Low (G3+ hypertension 4.8%, triglyceride elevation 3.6%, pneumothorax 2.4%; no treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: Pneumothorax risk from tumour cavitation in bilateral lung metastases; wound-healing impairment conflicts with metastasectomy.

overall: The best-looking VEGFR-TKI subset number in the file, from a non-prespecified 26-patient subgroup, in an arm that is currently suspended.

intervention_label: Brenetafusp (IMC-F106C, PRAME x CD3 ImmTAC) (NCT04262466)
expected_benefit: No peer-reviewed clinical publication exists for brenetafusp. The class precedent is tebentafusp, which moved overall survival in HLA-A*02:01-positive uveal melanoma, HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.37-0.71).
key_risks: Accrual is closed
Requires PRAME expression on the sponsor's own assay, unmeasured here
ImmTAC-class cytokine and skin toxicity, front-loaded over the first three to four doses
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO, because it is closed.
rationale_summary: The off-the-shelf version of the PRAME axis, and the one that would have avoided the leukapheresis and manufacturing delay that makes TCR-T hard to fit into any first-line window. It has stopped enrolling. Flagged not_enrollable and carried so the PRAME branch shows every door that was checked; the sponsor has an active PRAME programme, so one call about cohort reopening is not wasted.
open_questions: Whether any brenetafusp cohort is reopening or a successor PRAME study is registered
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: accrual closed, no peer-reviewed clinical publication for the agent; class precedent is uveal-melanoma-specific (pmid:34551229).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (ImmTAC-class rash, pyrexia and pruritus front-loaded over the first doses; class discontinuation for AE 2%)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen-loss and HLA LOH escape possible; no mechanism objection raised.

overall: The off-the-shelf PRAME route that needs no cell manufacturing, closed to accrual — one phone call away from being worth re-checking.

intervention_label: Valemetostat tosylate (EZH1/EZH2 dual inhibitor), SWI/SNF-defective basket cohort 1.A (NCT07303387)
scenario_label: If INI1/SMARCB1 loss is confirmed by IHC on tumour tissue (complete loss of nuclear staining with retained internal control), or biallelic molecular loss where IHC is equivocal
expected_benefit: No readout; phase 2 basket, antitumour activity as the endpoint. Approved in Japan for T-cell lymphoma; no FDA or EMA approval and investigational in solid tumours.
key_risks: Entry requires a documented biallelic homozygous SMARCB1 deletion by validated NGS plus centrally confirmed loss of expression by IHC; a single plasma frameshift satisfies neither
Four sites, all in France, with no US site as registered
ECOG 0-1 and a maximum of one prior treatment line in the SMARCB1 cohort
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO on geography and on the biomarker gate.
rationale_summary: A reader scanning the trial table sees a recruiting SMARCB1 study and assumes a door. Two things close it, and both are hard: the biallelic homozygous deletion requirement, which her heterozygous plasma frameshift does not come close to meeting, and France-only geography. Flagged not_enrollable rather than dropped so the SMARCB1 branch shows what was checked. If INI1 loss did confirm on tissue, the sequencing would be tight anyway, since cohort 1.A caps prior therapy at one line.
open_questions: Whether a truncating SMARCB1 frameshift with confirmed IHC loss would be accepted in place of homozygous deletion
Whether any US or EU site outside France is accepting international patients
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: France-only, and the protocol requires biallelic homozygous SMARCB1 deletion plus central IHC confirmation that a heterozygous plasma call cannot supply.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (EZH1/2 dual inhibition: thrombocytopenia, anaemia, dysgeusia in the lymphoma experience; no solid-tumour profile published)

counter_productive_moa.description: Same non-catalytic EZH2-dependency problem as tazemetostat, on a target the tissue may not carry.

overall: The live SWI/SNF basket that looks like a door and is not: biallelic homozygous deletion required, France only.

intervention_label: Tiragolumab + atezolizumab in SMARCB1- or SMARCA4-deficient tumours (NCT05286801)
scenario_label: If INI1/SMARCB1 loss is confirmed by IHC on tumour tissue (complete loss of nuclear staining with retained internal control), or biallelic molecular loss where IHC is equivocal
expected_benefit: No readout; phase 1/2 with dose-limiting toxicity and response as endpoints. Closed to accrual.
key_risks: Tiragolumab is investigational with no approval anywhere, so the combination cannot be assembled off protocol
Single-agent PD-L1 blockade in uterine LMS carries the same negative record as the other checkpoint rows
Closed to accrual across 40 sites
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO, because it is closed.
rationale_summary: Had it still been open, this was the most reachable SMARCB1-directed study for a US patient: its eligibility list ends with other SMARCB1- or SMARCA4-deficient tumours, an explicit histology-agnostic door, and institutional IHC was accepted as evidence. It closed to accrual. Flagged not_enrollable and kept visible because the INI1 result, if it ever comes back lost, should be waiting for whatever SWI/SNF study opens next.
open_questions: Whether the NCI study has any plan to reopen or add cohorts
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: closed to accrual, and the TIGIT partner is investigational with no off-protocol route.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (checkpoint-class immune-related toxicity; combination G3+ profile not published for this study)

counter_productive_moa.description: Checkpoint blockade has failed twice in this histology; TIGIT adds no evidence in sarcoma.

overall: The most reachable SMARCB1-directed study for a US patient until it closed to accrual — worth re-checking, not plannable.

intervention_label: Ubamatamab (MUC16 x CD3 bispecific), alone or with cemiplimab, in SMARCB1-deficient tumours (NCT06444880)
scenario_label: If INI1/SMARCB1 loss is confirmed by IHC on tumour tissue (complete loss of nuclear staining with retained internal control), or biallelic molecular loss where IHC is equivocal
expected_benefit: No readout; phase 2, n=15, safety and adverse events as the endpoint.
key_risks: Both cohorts are restricted to renal medullary carcinoma and epithelioid sarcoma, so her histology is excluded regardless of INI1 status
Closed to accrual
Requires MUC16 expression, untested and unlikely in this histology
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO; histology excludes her independently of enrolment status.
rationale_summary: Her histology is outside this twice over, and it is closed. Recorded so the SMARCB1 branch shows every door that was checked rather than leaving a reader to wonder whether a MUC16 bispecific was considered. Flagged not_enrollable.
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: histology-restricted to renal medullary carcinoma and epithelioid sarcoma, and closed to accrual.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (T-cell-engager CRS risk; no published grade profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection; the target antigen is unlikely to be present in this histology.

overall: A SMARCB1-platform study whose two cohorts exclude her histology, closed to accrual — checked and shut.

intervention_label: Afamitresgene autoleucel (MAGE-A4 TCR-T, TECELRA), SPEARHEAD-1
expected_benefit: ORR 37% (95% CI 24-51) by masked independent review in 52 patients with advanced synovial sarcoma or myxoid round-cell liposarcoma, 39% in the synovial subset. No leiomyosarcoma data.
key_risks: Cytokine release syndrome in 71% (one grade 3); G3+ lymphopenia 96% and neutropenia 85%; no treatment-related deaths
The TECELRA label reaches synovial sarcoma only, and an autologous engineered cell product is not something a clinician writes off-label the way they would a tablet
MAGE-A4 expression untested
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO. She clears the allele gate and nothing else.
guideline_status: Recognised in synovial sarcoma; no leiomyosarcoma recommendation anywhere.
rationale_summary: The clearest illustration in this case of why an HLA type is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. Her confirmed HLA-A*02:01 satisfies the restriction element; the label and the trial both stop at synovial sarcoma and myxoid round-cell liposarcoma, and authorised treatment centres order the product against the label indication and its companion diagnostic. Flagged not_enrollable. It should not be presented as an open option on the strength of the allele alone.
open_questions: Whether MAGE-A4 IHC, if positive, opens any basket TCR-T route in this histology
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: ORR 37% is synovial sarcoma and MRCLS (pmid:38554725); the label stops at synovial sarcoma and her histology is outside it.
toxicity_burden: High (CRS 71% with one G3; G3+ lymphopenia 96%, neutropenia 85%; no treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen-loss escape possible; no mechanism objection, the barrier is histology and label.

overall: Her HLA type clears the allele gate and nothing else — the label and the trial both stop at synovial sarcoma.

intervention_label: Uzatresgene autoleucel (ADP-A2M4CD8), alone or with checkpoint blockade (SURPASS, NCT04044859)
expected_benefit: No published readout; phase 1 with safety and tolerability endpoints. Closed to accrual.
key_risks: The eligible histology list covers urothelial, oesophageal, gastric, lung, head and neck, ovarian, endometrial and melanoma; a uterine sarcoma is not among them
Requires at least 90% room-air oxygen saturation at rest, measured at screening and again at baseline
Closed to new enrolment
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO on both histology and enrolment status.

It carries forward one criterion that matters more here than the enrolment status: at least 90% room-air saturation at rest, which is the class norm and the reason an oximetry reading with her altitude written on it is the free measurement that decides whether any of these seats are reachable.
open_questions: Whether any SURPASS cohort is reopening; the registry status reads active, not recruiting
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: closed to accrual and the histology list excludes uterine sarcoma.
toxicity_burden: High (TCR-T class: near-universal G3+ lymphodepletion cytopenias, CRS; no study-specific published profile)

overall: Closed, and its histology list excludes her — but its 90% room-air saturation criterion is the class gate her altitude makes decisive.

expected_benefit: The registrational results have no PubMed-indexed primary publication as of mid-2026. The citable evidence is the 12-patient NY-ESO-1c259 pilot in synovial sarcoma, confirmed ORR 50%.
key_risks: G3+ AEs in all 12 pilot patients, dominated by lymphodepletion cytopenias; CRS in 5 of 12 with two grade 3

Closed to accrual, and screening runs through a designated central laboratory

open_questions: Whether any IGNYTE-ESO cohort is reopening
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: synovial sarcoma and MRCLS only, closed to accrual; the citable efficacy is a 12-patient pilot (pmid:29891538).
toxicity_burden: High (G3+ AEs in all 12 pilot patients; lymphodepletion cytopenias, CRS in 5 of 12 with two G3)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen-loss escape possible; the barrier is histology restriction, and NY-ESO-1 is low across sarcoma subtypes.

overall: Histology-restricted and closed, on an antigen that stains low across sarcoma — order it only inside the shared panel.

intervention_label: Tebentafusp (gp100 x CD3 ImmTAC), HLA-A*02:01-restricted
expected_benefit: Overall survival HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.37-0.71) in previously untreated metastatic uveal melanoma. Everything else about it is uveal-melanoma-specific, since gp100 is a melanocytic antigen.
key_risks: Cytokine-mediated and skin toxicity dominate (rash 83%, pyrexia 76%, pruritus 69%), fading after the first three to four doses; discontinuation 2%
The label is uveal melanoma and the open sarcoma study is HMB-45-positive clear cell sarcoma only
That study excludes room-air oxygen saturation below 92%, the strictest oximetry threshold in this dossier
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO. Her allele fits and her tumour does not express the target.
rationale_summary: Carried as the class proof that an off-the-shelf HLA-A*02:01-restricted bispecific TCR can move overall survival in a solid tumour, which is what makes the PRAME ImmTAC and engager rows worth checking at all. Not reachable for her: gp100 is melanocytic and a leiomyosarcoma does not express it. Flagged not_enrollable. The one transferable detail is the 92% room-air saturation exclusion, which is the strictest in the class and should be settled at her own altitude before any T-cell-engager screening call.
open_questions: What oximetry threshold each engager protocol actually applies, and whether altitude annotation is accepted
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: gp100 is a melanocytic antigen absent from leiomyosarcoma; the OS result is uveal-melanoma-specific (pmid:34551229).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (rash 83%, pyrexia 76%, pruritus 69% any-grade, front-loaded; discontinuation for AE 2%, no treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: Target antigen absent in this histology; the row is class precedent, not a therapeutic proposal.

overall: The approved ImmTAC her allele fits and her tumour's biology does not — class precedent, plus the strictest oximetry threshold in the file.

T-cell-engager CRS risk with no published grade profile

intervention_label: MASCT-I (autologous dendritic cell and cytokine-induced killer cell therapy) + doxorubicin + ifosfamide, first line (NCT06277154)

The doxorubicin plus ifosfamide backbone carries febrile neutropenia at 46% despite pegfilgrastim
No efficacy evidence for the cell-therapy component in sarcoma
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO on geography.

expected_benefit: No readout; phase 2, n=45, objective response rate. The nearest published analogue is doxorubicin plus pembrolizumab first line, which missed its response endpoint (ORR 19%) while showing the combination is deliverable, mPFS 8.1 months and mOS 27.6 months.

open_questions: Whether any non-Chinese site exists
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: Shanghai single site. The nearest published analogue missed its response endpoint (ORR 19%, pmid:32910151).
toxicity_burden: High (anthracycline-ifosfamide backbone toxicity plus immune-related events; no combination profile published)

counter_productive_moa.description: Checkpoint blockade has failed twice in this histology; adding it to chemotherapy repeats a tested idea.

overall: A first-line chemo-immunotherapy seat in Shanghai, on a mechanism this disease has already defeated twice.

intervention_label: Fluzoparib + camrelizumab with concurrent SBRT to lung metastases (NCT06074692)
expected_benefit: No readout; phase 2, n=86, six-month progression-free survival rate.
key_risks: Single site in Shanghai, and neither fluzoparib nor camrelizumab is FDA-approved, so there is no off-label route
Requires at least one prior systemic line

preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) prefers_trials: NO on geography and on drug availability.
rationale_summary: The most interesting idea in this tier and the least reachable: it pairs PARP inhibition, the best lineage-matched mechanism in her case, with the lung-directed radiotherapy her oncologist has kept on the table. Single Shanghai site, and neither drug is available in the US. Flagged not_enrollable. The transferable part is not the protocol but the concept, and SBRT to lung lesions alongside systemic therapy can be pursued locally without it.
open_questions: Whether her pattern ever presents a definable SBRT target after induction
likelihood_of_effect: Not enrollable: Shanghai single site with two drugs unavailable in the US. Local SBRT carries its own retrospective evidence (pmid:37532104).
toxicity_burden: High (PARP-inhibitor myelosuppression plus checkpoint toxicity and concurrent radiotherapy; no combination profile published)

counter_productive_moa.description: Concurrent radiotherapy with a PARP inhibitor raises pneumonitis risk in already-infiltrated lung.

overall: The one protocol combining her best mechanism with her locoregional question, in Shanghai, with two drugs the US does not have.

intervention_label: Nivolumab monotherapy in uterine leiomyosarcoma
expected_benefit: Objective response rate 0% in the only uterine-LMS-specific single-agent PD-1 trial, stopped at stage 1 for futility after 12 patients, with median PFS 1.8 months.
key_risks: Grade 3+ events in 9 of 12 patients, though only 3 were attributed to nivolumab (abdominal pain, amylase/lipase rise, fatigue)
Prior PD-1 exposure would permanently close the ivonescimab seat
No biomarker in this case supports checkpoint blockade; MSI, MMR and TMB are all unmeasured
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7: NO. A 0% response rate fails on the efficacy side regardless of how tolerable it is.
guideline_status: Tumour-agnostic NCCN recognition exists for MSI-H/dMMR and TMB-high disease, and those routes sit in the Standard-of-care table gated on tissue testing she has not had. There is no sarcoma-specific recognition.
rationale_summary: One half of the case against single-agent checkpoint blockade here, and the half that is specific to her disease: a dedicated uterine LMS study stopped for futility at 0 of 12. The other half is SARC028, where the LMS cohort went 0 for 10 while UPS and dedifferentiated liposarcoma carried the signal. Not recommended as a strategy. Any checkpoint approach for her needs a combination rationale and a biomarker, and the biomarker questions (MSI, MMR, TMB) are closed cheaply on the block already being cut.
open_questions: Whether MMR IHC or tissue TMB returns anything that would reopen the tumour-agnostic route
likelihood_of_effect: Low for response: ORR 0% with mPFS 1.8 months in the only dedicated uLMS PD-1 trial, stopped for futility (pmid:28440953).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ events in 9 of 12, three attributed to drug: abdominal pain, amylase/lipase rise, fatigue)

counter_productive_moa.description: Prior PD-1 exposure permanently closes the ivonescimab seat and buys nothing this histology has shown it responds to.

overall: The negative result that defines the checkpoint question in this disease: 0 of 12, stopped for futility.

intervention_label: Nivolumab +/- ipilimumab, dual checkpoint blockade in sarcoma (Alliance A091401)
expected_benefit: Confirmed ORR 16% (95% CI 7-30) in the combination arm of a randomised non-comparative phase 2 in 85 patients with metastatic sarcoma after at least one prior line; the authors sent the combination forward rather than the monotherapy.
key_risks: Combination arm G3+ anaemia 19% and hypotension 10%; treatment-related serious AEs 26% versus 19% with monotherapy
No uterine LMS efficacy breakdown; the histology's own single-agent record is 0 of 12 and 0 of 10
Prior checkpoint exposure closes the ivonescimab seat
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7: NO for this histology, in the absence of a biomarker.
guideline_status: No sarcoma-specific guideline recognition for the combination.
rationale_summary: The one piece of evidence that dual checkpoint blockade retrieves a modest response rate in sarcoma where PD-1 alone fails, which is why it supports combination or bispecific logic more than any single-agent plan. It does not rescue the histology: no uterine LMS breakdown exists, and the two negative uLMS-relevant trials remain the nearest data. Not recommended without a biomarker, and the biomarker work is on the rank-1 block cut.
open_questions: Whether MSI, dMMR or high TMB returns and changes the calculus
Whether any published LMS-specific breakdown of the combination exists
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-uncertain: ORR 16% across sarcoma histologies with no uLMS breakdown, against a 0-of-12 and 0-of-10 record in this disease (pmid:29370992).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (G3+ anaemia 19%, hypotension 10%; treatment-related serious AEs 26%; no treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: Repeats a mechanism this histology has twice defeated, and forecloses the ivonescimab seat on the way.

overall: The evidence that dual blockade beats single-agent PD-1 in sarcoma generally, with nothing in it specific to uterine leiomyosarcoma.

intervention_label: Doxorubicin + pembrolizumab, first-line chemo-immunotherapy (phase 1/2)
expected_benefit: Objective response rate 19% (primary endpoint not met) in 37 anthracycline-naive sarcoma patients, LMS the most common subtype at 11 of 37; mPFS 8.1 months (95% CI 7.6-10.8) and mOS 27.6 months (95% CI 18.7-NR).
key_risks: Durable responses clustered in UPS and dedifferentiated liposarcoma rather than LMS
Choosing it first line trades the only randomised OS result in this disease for a regimen whose response endpoint failed
Prior PD-1 exposure closes the ivonescimab seat
preference_alignment: Matches the (defaulted) efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.7: NO. It is deliverable, but the efficacy case against LMS-04 does not hold.
guideline_status: No guideline carriage for the combination.
rationale_summary: The most useful thing this row does is mark the boundary of the chemo-immunotherapy question in the first-line window. The combination is deliverable, with no dose-limiting toxicities and PFS and OS that compare well with historical doxorubicin, but its response endpoint failed and its durable responders were not leiomyosarcomas. Against a regimen with mOS 33 versus 24 months and PFS HR 0.41 in her disease, that is not a trade the board could defend, and none of them ranked it.
open_questions: Whether any prospective chemo-immunotherapy study enriches for LMS with a biomarker rather than by histology
likelihood_of_effect: Low for response: ORR 19% with the primary endpoint missed, durable responses clustered outside LMS (pmid:32910151).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (no dose-limiting toxicities reported; anthracycline myelosuppression plus immune-related events, no per-term G3 table published)

counter_productive_moa.description: Spends the first-line window and the anthracycline budget on a mechanism this histology has not responded to.

overall: Deliverable first-line chemo-immunotherapy whose response endpoint failed and whose responders were other histologies.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition on the ATRX / ALT hypothesis (berzosertib, tuvusertib class)
expected_benefit: The ATRX-mutant leiomyosarcoma cohort of the molecularly selected berzosertib phase 2 progressed within 4 months despite biopsy-proven pharmacodynamic target engagement; the longest disease control in that study was in SDH-mutant GIST. SLFN11, not ATRX, tracked with benefit.
key_risks: The underlying preclinical claim that ALT-positive cells are selectively ATR-inhibitor sensitive failed to replicate
No ATR inhibitor is approved anywhere
The randomised leiomyosarcoma-specific test of gemcitabine with or without ATR inhibition completed accrual in France and is unreported

The thesis was tested in her exact histology, in patients selected for the exact biomarker the preclinical file proposes, with target engagement demonstrated on serial biopsy, and they progressed within 4 months. The conservative and the critic both named it in their round-1 notes as a branch they would not spend a line on. ATRX is still worth reporting from tissue order A because it informs biology and diagnosis, but ordering it is not the same as ranking the drug class. Not recommended.
open_questions: Whether the accrued randomised berzosertib plus gemcitabine leiomyosarcoma study reports anything that revives the class
Whether SLFN11, rather than ATRX or ALT, is the marker worth measuring if the class is ever revisited
likelihood_of_effect: Low: the hypothesis was tested in ATRX-mutant LMS with proven target engagement and patients progressed within 4 months (pmid:39453756).
toxicity_burden: Moderate (ATR-inhibitor class myelosuppression; monotherapy profile from the negative phase 2)

counter_productive_moa.description: ALT-selective ATR sensitivity failed to replicate; selecting on ATRX rather than SLFN11 is selecting on the wrong marker.

overall: The one hypothesis in this case that has already been tested in her histology with the right biomarker and the right pharmacodynamics, and lost.

intervention_label: PARP inhibition in BRCA2-altered uterine leiomyosarcoma (genomic series)
expected_benefit: Four of four BRCA2-altered uterine LMS patients had durable clinical benefit on PARP inhibition in a retrospective genomic analysis plus case series. No systematic adverse-event reporting.

The critic's caution is the right frame — a 4-patient series is tier 4 and hypothesis-generating, so it supports ordering a test, not selecting a therapy.
open_questions: Her tumour and germline HRR status, both unmeasured
Whether a germline finding, which the validator flagged as a separate high-priority order, strengthens the off-label authorisation

toxicity_burden: Low (no systematic AE reporting in a four-patient off-label series; class profile carried on the rank-2 row)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism objection; the risk is over-reading a four-patient series as a selection rule.

overall: The reason BRCA2 belongs on her tissue order, and a four-patient series that cannot carry more weight than that.

expected_benefit: Not a therapy. The prevalence series carried here spans bone and soft-tissue sarcoma including 26 smooth-muscle tumours, is not uterus-restricted, puts PRAME highest in UPS and osteosarcoma, quotes no smooth-muscle PRAME figure, and its adjacent MAGE-A4 smooth-muscle number drew an erratum and is flagged internally inconsistent in this dossier's own row.

Antigen expression in all three targets is untested

The claim that PRAME is the likeliest of the three antigens to return positive has nothing under it in this file, and the one series that could have supported it does not report a smooth-muscle PRAME figure. Tumour HLA-A*02:01 loss of heterozygosity, which tissue order A can report at no additional time if requested

intervention_label: Checkpoint-blockade target biology in uterine leiomyosarcoma (immune classes, tertiary lymphoid structures, pS6-high sensitisation)
expected_benefit: Not a therapy. The mechanistic work suggests where checkpoint blockade could work in sarcoma — B-cell-rich, tertiary-lymphoid-structure-high immune classes, and PI3K/mTOR inhibition sensitising pS6-high uterine LMS to PD-1 blockade — against a clinical record in this histology of 0 of 10 and 0 of 12.

PD-L1 gates no approval in soft-tissue sarcoma, so a stain informs rather than decides

What it does earn is the immune-phenotype half of the rank-1 tissue order, since the lung lesions were read as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory and nobody has looked at whether that corresponds to an immune infiltrate.

MSI, MMR and TMB, all unmeasured, which are what would actually open checkpoint blockade here
